To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Habits, action sequences, and reinforcement learning.

(1) the distinction between goal-directed and habitual behaviour can be accounted for in terms of a single reinforcement learning model; (2) the distinction between the two types of behaviour is based on the number of actions in the sequence; (3) this approach is consistent with what real organisms do; (4) it generates new predictions about the nature of habit formation and extinction; and (5) it has implications for the way we should be thinking about habit in the future.
the development of habitual action can be explained by the same learning mechanisms that explain goal-directed action, but only if we reconceptualize habits as action sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of habits and their role in human behaviour.
the nature of habit formation and the mechanisms by which they are regulated.
the nature of habits and the way they develop in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
habits are not model-free but rather a special case of model-based RL.
the current model of instrumental conditioning is incomplete.
model-free RL is unnecessary and that habits are best understood as action sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distinction between goal-directed and habitual behaviour is best described by the distinction between actions and action sequences.
habits, as action sequences, can be explained by model-based RL.
habits are not a distinct class of action but rather a particular type of action sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the model-free approach to habit formation is unnecessary and that the model-based approach can explain the formation and maintenance of habits as well as the more familiar model-based approach to goal-directed action.
model-based RL can explain all aspects of goal-directed and habitual action, and that model-free RL is not required.
habits are not a separate controller, but are simply a particular type of goal-directed action sequence.
